- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots next period — cap forecast at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.5) and price is trending up, model may overestimate momentum — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive, model often lags — forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% in first 2–3 periods.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 5+ days, model tends to overestimate continuation — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment is flat (±0.1–0.3) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise — use 30-day moving average as baseline for correction.
